questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I found that Portugal was a country that I did not know that much about, even though it has been a country with big historical impact, both in an European and international context.

However, since Portugal is in the EU I found it to be much easier to go on exchange here, compared to going outside of EU.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had an excellent stay, and found people to very welcoming. In addition to this, it was very easy to meet people to hang out with, since there were so many other exchange students.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was many informations regarding social Erasmus activities. However it should be noted, that it said on the internet that you had to reserve a spot for all of the activities weeks in advance, when in practice, you could sign up for many activities the day before. This could have saved me for some money, since I ended up not attending some of the social activities since they often overlapped.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university did not provide that many informations. It's important to come to the first orientation at NOVA, but also to discuss things with the other students if there's anything you're in doubt about.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I was in a special situation, since my girlfriend was supposed to join me after the first 2 1/2 months. That meant, that I had to find accommodation for the both of us. 

I had not found anything beforehand, and I thus had to find something after I arrived. There were many scammers on Facebook, so take care. 

I ended up finding something together through some canadian exchange students I meet during the intro week. So just as in most cases, connections was key.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
The cost of housing is surprisingly high. Many of my friends stayed in small rooms for about 400-500 euro a month. I lived in an apartment with my girlfriend for 1200 euro a month. 

This has to be taken into account that the average wage in Lisbon is around 800 euro a month.

I would strongly recommend living in Lisbon instead of Cascais where the university is. Sure, you will save some time in train going to NOVA, but most things happen in the city, and then you don't have to thing about when the last train is going, if you're out partying or just out to eat.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
There are some good sites to find accommodation, among others I would recommend

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
A problem with their system is, that they don't tell you when courses don't have any more available spots left. 
This was a problem during my betting fase, since I spent a lot of time, trying to get on a specific course.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Their system is set up like a betting system. You have 100 virtual coins, and then you bet the amount on each course that you want to attend. If you bid higher than others, you get on the course.

There are multiple betting rounds though, so if you don't get your first priority you can bet on something else. You can also change your mind, and drop a course and get your coins back to bet on something else. 

Be aware that you can't have overlapping classes, since class participation is part of the grade.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Satisfactory level of help. There was explanation on the intro day, but there was also a pdf explanation when going on to the side to bet on courses. It's a quick navigation tour but it's sufficient.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I only took 14 ECTS, since that was all I had left of my studies besides my thesis.

I unfortunately only got one of my first priorities (the courses are 7 or 3.5 ECTS for master students), but then I got my second and third priorities. I took courses that some of my friend I meet in the intro week also took, so that we could arrange group work together. I can recommend doing that.

Otherwise there is also primarily foreign students at master level, so it's relatively easy to meet someone at class to talk to as well.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be quick to sign up for classes. Bet high on your most important courses. Sometimes the courses are filled up, however that won't be stated, since people can sign off courses as well. I would advise betting high in the first round, and if you then don't get a spot on a course, you need to go after something else. If it's an attractive course there is a high probability that there is no more spots left.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two courses. One of the courses had a level comparable to UCPH, however the other course had much lower level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It's quite different. Class participation is part of the grade, so people will participate much more that what I was used to. In addition to this, there is also midterms in many courses. The teachers wanted to learn students names.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Banking and Data Analytics for Finance

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Data Analytics for Finance was a relatively tough course where you could potentially learn a lot. However, there was an assignment every second week, a midterm as well as a final project, so it will take a lot of work.

Banking was a very easy course, however not very interesting in my opinion. However, it can be registered as a seminar, which is a much much easier way to do it, compared to doing a seminar at UCPH. 

My workload was 80/20 between the two courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I ended up eating out a lot more than expected. However, it's a good way to be together with other Erasmus students, since most students don't have a place where they can invite people over. 

You have to get the yellow, monthly transportation card, it saves many headaches and is also very cheap compared to how far you can get on it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food was also more expensive that expected, cheaper than Copenhagen, but not by that much.

However if you go to some bars at Bairro Alto, it's a lot cheaper than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: NOVA has a football club you can sign up for. There is also many activities regarding surfing. There is also a monthly friday party.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Try to sign up for surfing. It's challenging and demanding, but very fun, and very cheap compared to what you would expect.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If you get the yellow travel card, you can go very way. Sintra is a very popular travel goal. However I would also go south and visit Sesimbra and Setúbal

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: People are generally quite good at English, and people are used to foreigners. I found it easy to adjust. People from the southern part of Portugal is very friendly but also more reserved than in the north, where they are more like spanish or Italian people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It's difficult to meet Portuguese people. But be open and be sure to get people you meets WhatsApp number, so you can keep in touch if you meet someone nice.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy to adjust. One thing however, is that the tempo is very slow. Often there is long lines since people take their time, and you can expect to wait a lot longer than expected on the bus or tram.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very friendly. They are also where down to earth, and are not afraid to celebrate.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go on day trips and explore cities around Lisboa. 

Get the monthly train card as quickly as possible. However, the wait time is very long. It's at Marques du Pombal train station. Get help from someone that speaks Portuguese/spanish or use google translate

Live in Lisbon, not Carcavelos.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The clubs are for free for NOVA students at Thursdays.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The city is very beautiful. It's run down but very charming. People are very nice. It was a great experience to go abroad where I had no expectations or obligations, I could just explore and be impulsive.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding accommodation, I stayed the first 4 weeks in a hostel

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
